about: Topic packs written by the scheduled routine. Every slug here, and every slug in ../topics.json, is taken: later runs must pick new topics from BACKLOG.md and pass check.mjs.

topics.title: Letting go of people-pleasing
topics.description: For learning to say no and stop shaping yourself around other people's approval.
topics.firstLine: People-pleasing usually started as a clever way to stay safe. Over the next ninety days you get to decide whether it still serves you.

topics.title: Changing careers
topics.description: For leaving one line of work and growing into the next.
topics.firstLine: Leaving one kind of work for another is a big move. It makes sense that part of you feels unsteady right now.

topics.title: Starting over in a new place
topics.description: For building a life, and a new sense of self, after a move.
topics.firstLine: Moving somewhere new takes more out of a person than most people admit. If you are tired in a way sleep does not fix, that makes sense.

topics.title: From putting off to doing
topics.description: For outgrowing procrastination and becoming someone who starts and finishes.
topics.firstLine: Putting things off is not a character flaw. It is usually a way of protecting yourself from a feeling you would rather not have.

topics.title: Quieting self-doubt
topics.description: For outgrowing a harsh inner critic and growing into quieter confidence.
topics.firstLine: The voice that tells you that you are not enough has been talking a long time. For the next few months, you get to talk back, gently.

topics.title: Becoming someone who moves
topics.description: For growing into a person who walks, stretches and exercises, at any age or fitness level.
topics.firstLine: You have spent years thinking of yourself as not the sporty type. This is a quiet invitation to try on a different story, one day at a time.

topics.title: Good enough is good: easing perfectionism
topics.description: For loosening impossible standards and finishing things kindly.
topics.firstLine: Wanting things done well is a good quality. Over the next ninety days, you get to find out where it helps you and where it quietly wears you down.

topics.title: Getting out of your head
topics.description: For outgrowing rumination and replaying, and coming back to the present.
topics.firstLine: If your mind tends to run the same thoughts round and round, you are not alone. Over the next ninety days you can practise stepping out of the loop.

topics.title: Stopping the comparison habit
topics.description: For measuring your life by your own values instead of other people’s highlights.
topics.firstLine: Comparing yourself to others is one of the oldest human habits. Over the next ninety days you can learn to loosen its grip, one ordinary day at a time.

topics.title: Becoming calm and steady with money
topics.description: For growing a steadier, less anxious relationship with money (habits and feelings, not financial advice).
topics.firstLine: Money stirs up strong feelings for almost everyone. Over the next ninety days you can grow a calmer, steadier relationship with it.

topics.title: Becoming a morning person
topics.description: For gently shifting your days earlier and growing into someone who enjoys mornings.
topics.firstLine: You do not have to become a different species to enjoy mornings. You just need a few kind changes, tried slowly, over the next few months.

topics.title: Holding boundaries with family
topics.description: For saying what you need with the people who know you longest.
topics.firstLine: Family can be the people who know you best and the people who push hardest on your limits. Both can be true at once.

topics.title: Taking back your attention
topics.description: For outgrowing compulsive phone and screen habits and choosing where your attention goes.
topics.firstLine: Your attention is one of the few things that is truly yours. Over the next ninety days or so, you will slowly take more of it back, one small choice at a time.

topics.title: Becoming slower to anger
topics.description: For outgrowing a quick temper and growing into a calmer, steadier you.
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, you will practise becoming slower to anger. Not a different person, just a steadier version of the one you already are.

topics.title: Making things again
topics.description: For returning to a creative practice after years away.
topics.firstLine: For years you may have told yourself you are not creative anymore. Over the next ninety or so days, we will test that story gently, one small made thing at a time.

topics.title: Learning to enjoy your own company
topics.description: For growing comfortable, even content, with time on your own.
topics.firstLine: Being on your own can feel awkward, even uneasy. Over roughly ninety days, these notes will help you discover that your own company can be a place of rest.

topics.title: Building new friendships as an adult
topics.description: For becoming someone who reaches out, follows up and keeps friends.
topics.firstLine: Friendships in adult life rarely just happen; they get built, one small contact at a time. These notes will keep you company for about ninety days while you build yours.

topics.title: Becoming your own boss
topics.description: For growing into self-employment (habits and feelings, not financial or legal advice).
topics.firstLine: Going from employee to your own boss is as much an inner shift as a practical one. For roughly ninety days, these short notes will help you grow into that new role.

topics.title: Outgrowing jealousy in relationships
topics.description: For feeling more secure and less consumed by jealousy with the people you love.
topics.firstLine: Jealousy can make love feel like a test you are always about to fail. For about ninety days, these notes will help you build a calmer, more secure footing in the relationships that matter to you.

topics.title: Loosening the need for control
topics.description: For easing your grip on people, plans and outcomes.
topics.firstLine: Holding tightly to plans, people and outcomes can be exhausting. Across roughly ninety days, these notes invite you to loosen your grip a finger at a time and see what happens.

topics.title: From complaining to changing
topics.description: For outgrowing habitual complaining and moving towards action and acceptance.
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, you will practise moving from complaining towards changing what you can and accepting what you cannot. You are not being asked to pretend everything is fine.

topics.title: Becoming a reader again
topics.description: For growing back into someone who reads books for pleasure.
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, you will practise becoming a reader again. Not a speed reader or a book collector, just someone who finds their way back to the page.

topics.title: Becoming a lifelong learner
topics.description: For learning a new skill as an adult and outgrowing too old, not the type.
topics.firstLine: For about ninety days, these notes will help you take up learning again as a grown-up. You do not need a classroom or a certificate, only a little curiosity and a few minutes most days.

topics.title: Becoming an organised person
topics.description: For calmer home and admin habits, and fewer last-minute scrambles.
topics.firstLine: Across roughly ninety days, these notes will help you build a calmer, tidier relationship with your home and your admin. No overhaul needed, just small steady habits.

topics.title: Becoming a better listener
topics.description: For growing into someone who listens fully, interrupts less and makes people feel heard.
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, these short notes will help you become a better listener. Not a silent one, just someone who lets other people finish and feel properly heard.

topics.title: Growing into your first leadership role
topics.description: For the shift from doing the work to leading people who do it.
topics.firstLine: Stepping from doing the work to leading the people who do it is a real shift. Over roughly the next ninety days, these short notes will keep you company as you grow into it.

topics.title: Becoming someone who cooks for themselves
topics.description: For growing from takeaways and skipped meals into someone who cooks simple food at home (not diet advice).
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, these short notes will help you become someone who cooks for themselves. Not a chef, just a person who can make a simple meal at home and enjoy it.

topics.title: Finding yourself again as a new parent
topics.description: For holding on to who you are while growing into being a parent.
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, these short notes will keep you company as you grow into being a parent while holding on to who you are. Read them whenever you can; there is no wrong time.

topics.title: When the children leave home
topics.description: For rediscovering yourself, your days and your relationships once the children have grown and gone.
topics.firstLine: Over roughly the next ninety days, these short notes will keep you company as the house grows quieter. One a day, to help you find out who you are now the children have flown.

topics.title: Starting retirement with purpose
topics.description: For growing into life after work with structure, meaning and connection (not financial advice).
topics.firstLine: Welcome to the start of something new. Over roughly ninety days, these brief notes will help you shape a life after work that feels purposeful, structured and connected.

topics.title: The year after graduating
topics.description: For finding your footing, identity and direction in the first year out of education (not career or financial advice).
topics.firstLine: The first year after education can feel strangely shapeless, even lonely. Over roughly ninety days, these notes will help you find your footing and a sense of who you are becoming.

topics.title: Growing into midlife
topics.description: For meeting midlife with curiosity rather than dread, and growing into who you are next.
topics.firstLine: Arriving at midlife can stir up a quiet dread, or a sense that the best chapters are behind you. Over roughly ninety days, these notes will help you meet this stage with curiosity and grow into who you are next.

topics.title: Treating yourself with respect
topics.description: For keeping promises to yourself, speaking to yourself kindly and expecting decent treatment.
topics.firstLine: Respecting yourself can feel unfamiliar, even a little uncomfortable at first. Over roughly ninety days, these notes will help you keep your word to yourself, speak to yourself kindly and expect decent treatment.

topics.title: Letting go of an old grudge
topics.description: For loosening resentment's hold for your own sake, without excusing harm or needing reconciliation.
topics.firstLine: Holding onto an old hurt can feel like guarding something important. Over roughly ninety days, these notes will help you loosen a grudge's grip for your own sake, without excusing what happened.

topics.title: Learning to ask for help
topics.description: For outgrowing doing everything alone and becoming someone who can ask for and accept support.
topics.firstLine: Doing everything yourself can feel like safety, even pride. Over the next ninety or so days, these notes will help you practise letting other people share the load.

topics.title: Noticing what is good
topics.description: For an honest gratitude habit, not forced positivity: you can feel bad and grateful at once.
topics.firstLine: Gratitude does not mean pretending everything is fine. Over roughly ninety days, these notes will help you notice what is good alongside whatever is hard.
